variants.answer: I’d treat each new comment as an event and first verify that the post owner wants email notifications and that the commenter isn’t the owner. I’d write the comment and an outbox event in the same database transaction, then have workers process the outbox. For deduplication, I’d give each notification a stable key, such as recipient + comment ID + notification type, and enforce a unique constraint on it; retries would reuse that key. To avoid flooding, I’d aggregate comments per recipient and post over a short window—for example, send one email after five minutes saying “3 new comments,” then include links to each comment. I’d also cap frequency, defer low-priority mail, honor unsubscribes and bounces, and offer immediate notifications as a preference. I’d monitor duplicate-send rate, queue delay, and emails per user. In a rollout, I’d compare those metrics against a baseline; for example, a target could be fewer than 0.1% duplicate notifications and no recipient receiving more than one digest per post per window.

variants.answer: I’d create a notification when a comment is saved, then send it through a background queue so a mail outage doesn’t affect commenting. I’d use a unique notification ID to make retries idempotent and avoid sending the same alert twice. To reduce volume, I’d batch comments on the same post into a digest and add per-user rate limits and notification preferences. I’d track delivery failures and how many emails each user receives, then adjust the batching window if people still get too many messages.
